hook: A hectare of farmland just outside Rotterdam can cost many times what a hectare costs on the cattle lands of Patagonia. That price gap shapes what farmers grow: costly land near a market must earn a lot, so it is farmed intensively, while cheap, distant land is used for grazing.

prereq.q: Which kind of agriculture spreads few inputs over large areas?
prereq.why: Extensive agriculture uses few inputs per hectare, as in ranching.

prereq.q: A map shows data for each province of one country. What is its scale of analysis?
prereq.why: The scale of analysis is the scale of the data: provinces are parts of a country.

figure.caption: Near the market, market gardening can pay the most rent; grain wins the middle distances and ranching the farthest.

chain.cause: Many land users want land with easy access to a market
chain.effect: land near the market costs more

chain.cause: Land near the market costs more
chain.effect: only uses that earn a lot per hectare can afford it

chain.cause: Market gardening earns the most per hectare but loses value fast with distance
chain.effect: market gardens take land closest to the market

chain.cause: Ranching earns little per hectare but ships cheaply
chain.effect: ranching takes the cheapest, most distant land

ideas: Subsistence agriculture feeds the farm family (rice plots in Bangladesh); commercial agriculture sells for profit (soybeans in Mato Grosso, Brazil).
Monocropping grows the same crop on a field year after year, and monoculture one crop over a large area: efficient, but risky if pests, drought or prices strike.
Bid-rent theory: land near a market costs more, so the use that can pay most wins it. Intensive uses take the center, extensive uses the edges. It assumes one market and equal transport.

misconception.wrong: Subsistence means extensive, and commercial means intensive.
misconception.right: Subsistence and commercial describe purpose (eat or sell); intensive and extensive describe inputs per hectare. A Bangladesh rice paddy is subsistence and intensive; an Argentine ranch is commercial and extensive.

summary: Subsistence agriculture feeds the farm family; commercial agriculture sells for profit and often uses monocropping. Bid-rent theory explains why intensive uses take costly land near a market and extensive uses take cheap, distant land, though real regions with many markets and routes depart from it.
